messages:
maya: Noticed mismatch in /generate endpoint docs: example body uses `temperature` as a string in the JS snippet (`"0.7"`) but schema expects a number. Opened a quick PR to correct examples.

docbot: PR created: docs#460 by maya (CI: running)

nikhil: Oof, that will break runtime validation in many examples. Also found a Ruby snippet using `temp:` symbol key instead of `temperature`. We should standardize all language snippets.

jen: I can run a quick grep across docs and generate a list of files to patch. Suggest we add a small linter rule to catch typed-literal mismatches in examples going forward.

maya: I updated JS and curl examples to use numeric temperature and fixed the Ruby sample locally. Pushed commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/commit/patch-temp-number

nikhil: One more: response schema in the reference shows `tokens: string[]` but actual server emits `tokens: [{text: string, idx: number}]`. We should update the schema to the richer shape and add an example of iterating tokens in Node.

jen: Added a note in the migration guide for anyone parsing tokens as strings. Also added the Node snippet showing `for (const t of response.tokens) console.log(t.idx, t.text)`

docbot: CI passed for docs#460 and docs#461. Merged.

maya: Thanks — I'll add a brief changelog entry and file a follow-up to add the linter rule for example type checks.
